paper_title: WaFFLe: Gated Cache-Ways with Per-Core Fine-Grained DVFS for Reduced On-Chip Temperature and Leakage Consumption

extraction.paper_title: WaFFLe: Gated Cache-Ways with Per-Core Fine-Grained DVFS for Reduced On-Chip Temperature and Leakage Consumption

scenario.figure_or_table: Table 1 (system parameters) with Fig. 13 (16-tile floorplan), Fig. 16 (peak temperature) and Table 3 (8MB LLC comparison)
scenario.description: WaFFLe combined LLC way-shutdown plus per-core fine-grained DVFS on a 16-tile homogeneous CMP, evaluated on nine PARSEC applications. The headline result is an 8.4 C reduction in peak temperature and a 6.2 C reduction in average temperature versus baseline (8MB LLC), with 2.5% average IPS degradation. The paper reports no block coordinates, dimensions or per-block wattages in text, only tile layout figures and per-block temperature maps (Fig. 20 for Black).
scenario.architecture: 16-tile homogeneous tiled CMP in 2D (32nm); each tile has an Alpha 21364 out-of-order core with private 64KB L1-I and 64KB L1-D, one bank of a shared SNUCA L2/LLC (1MB 16-way per bank, 8MB total in the main evaluation), and a 2D-mesh NoC router. Per-core on-chip voltage regulators at 20 mV/ns. Simulated with gem5, McPAT and HotSpot 6.0; the HotFloorPlan module generates the floorplan from McPAT area estimates.
scenario.workload: PARSEC multi-threaded benchmark suite, large inputs, 16 threads (one per core), RoI only, 80M cycles; all cores always active
scenario.operating_point: Baseline 1.12 V / 3.0 GHz, FG-DVFS low state 0.76 V / 1.2 GHz during LLC-miss stalls; ambient 47 C; thermal interval 0.33 us; way-shutdown interval 2M cycles; POWER_DOWN=0.025, POWER_UP=0.04; DRAM latency 70 ns

original_setup.solver: gem5 full-system simulator with McPAT (32nm power/area) and HotSpot 6.0 (HotFloorPlan generates the floorplan from McPAT area estimates). Leakage is recomputed per component from the previous interval's temperature, in 0.33 us periods (PDF p.12-13).
original_setup.optimizer: No numerical optimizer. The policy is a heuristic with two parts: threshold-based LLC way-shutdown (POWER_DOWN=0.025, POWER_UP=0.04, 2M-cycle interval, clean non-MRU intra-set migration) and an LLC-miss-triggered DVFS rule (Algorithms 1 and 2, PDF p.5-6, 11, 13).
original_setup.controller: WaFFLe combined controller. The LLC controller gates cache-ways per bank from the miss ratio. A per-core FG-DVFS controller switches between 1.12 V/3.0 GHz and 0.76 V/1.2 GHz on global isolated LLC misses detected in the LLC directory. On-chip regulators switch at 20 mV/ns (PDF p.8-11, 14).
original_setup.benchmark: Nine multi-threaded PARSEC applications (large inputs, 16 threads, RoI, 80M cycles) on a 16-tile homogeneous CMP with an 8MB LLC (1MB 16-way per bank). Baselines and comparisons: baseline, WS_OPT, FG-DVFS alone, and GDP1/GDP2 (bank shutdown plus greedy DVFS) (PDF p.12-14, 22).

thermal_observable.unit: degC (reduction in peak temperature vs. baseline)
thermal_observable.location: Peak (hottest on-chip point) over the 16-tile CMP, 8MB LLC configuration (cores and caches); the reported maximum is across the nine PARSEC applications
thermal_observable.aggregation: Maximum reduction in peak temperature across the nine PARSEC applications. The per-application range is 6.5-8.4 C. The paper reports the same figure as the Table 3 headline (8MB LLC) and in the abstract. Average temperature reduction is 6.2 C.

physical_mismatches.reason: The paper's workload is transient and dynamic. Cache ways are gated at 2M-cycle intervals, per-core DVFS switches during memory stalls at ns scale, and temperature is traced at 0.33 us. A steady 2D thermal runner with a one-row power trace cannot reproduce this time-varying behavior.

The controller and optimizer (way-shutdown and FG-DVFS algorithms, directory-based miss detection, performance/IPS feedback) are architectural policies. Their effect depends on gem5 and McPAT performance and power traces, which are not available in a Studio thermal solve.

The paper publishes no block coordinates, dimensions, or per-block wattages. The floorplan is generated by HotFloorPlan from McPAT areas and is shown only as tile figures (Fig. 13, Fig. 20) and temperature maps. No same-scenario block geometry and power rows can be built from the paper without digitizing or inventing values.

The reported observable is a temperature reduction relative to the paper's own baseline, not an absolute temperature. It depends on HotSpot 6.0 package and cooling parameters that the paper does not publish except for a 47 C ambient. Studio package and cooling assumptions cannot be matched, so temperatures are not numerically comparable.

Dynamic power gating of LLC ways is modeled as a time-varying change in power and leakage with temperature feedback (component-wise leakage from the previous period's temperature). A static Studio power map has no such coupling.
The paper is a 2D tiled CMP with no 3D stacking, interposer, or chiplets. This is a mismatch with 3D and interposer thermal tools but not a blocker for a 2D scenario.

studio_assumptions: No complete experiment is extractable, so the floorplan is empty. If an illustrative run were made, any generated 2D placement and one-row power trace would be separate from paper facts, and its temperatures would not be compared numerically to the paper.
Studio package and material properties (die, TIM, heat spreader, heat sink, convection) are bundled defaults and not the paper's HotSpot 6.0 configuration, which is not published.
Ambient is the only paper-stated thermal boundary condition (47 C, Table 1, PDF p.13). Other boundary conditions would be Studio defaults.
missing_inputs: Block coordinates (x_m, y_m) and dimensions (width_m, height_m) for cores, L1 caches, L2 banks, and routers. Only tile layout figures (Fig. 13, p.12; Fig. 20, p.16) appear, with no numeric geometry, and the HotFloorPlan output is not provided.

Per-block power values in watts for any scenario. McPAT outputs are not published. Only regulator power (0.106 W at 0.76 V, 0.168 W at 1.12 V per core, PDF p.14) and stall-period core energies (337 nJ baseline, 86-94 nJ with FG-DVFS, p.10) are given, and these cannot be split into block powers.
Power time series or traces from gem5/McPAT.
HotSpot 6.0 package, material, cooling, and boundary-condition configuration (heat spreader, heat sink, TIM, convection resistance, die thickness).
Absolute baseline and WaFFLe temperatures are given only in Fig. 20 (Black), where per-block values (e.g. 373.83 K) are legible only as figure text and are not tied to a tabulated source.
No linked repositories, code, configs, or supplementary assets: artifact search found no links and the packet assets list is empty.

methods.note: The gem5 + McPAT + HotSpot 6.0 pipeline, the Algorithm 1 and 2 policies, the 0.33 us thermal interval and the 2M-cycle way-shutdown interval are described in the supplied text (pp.5-6, 8-11, 13). The extraction correctly says this is a transient, architectural, policy-driven study and not a steady 2D case. Paper-level inconsistencies remain: the 13 ns regulator time disagrees with 20 mV/ns, and 500 thermal stamps span only about 165 us versus a 2M-cycle interval.

findings.reason: The extraction states 1MB 16-way per bank and 8MB total. With 16 tiles each holding one L2 bank, 1MB per bank gives 16MB, and Sec. 5.4 treats 16MB as a separate larger LLC. The paper never shows how 8MB maps onto 16 banks (0.5MB each?). The 8MB headline scenario is therefore not reconciled with Table 1 and Figs. 2, 4, 5 (1MB banks).
findings.locator: PDF p.13 Table 1 'L2 1MB, 16-way'; p.6 Fig. 2/3 captions; p.14 Sec. 5.1; p.18 Sec. 5.4; p.22 Table 3 caption

findings.reason: The values 373.83, 368.20, 362.58, 356.95, 351.33, 345.70, 340.08, 336.33 (and 366.59, 361.69, 356.80, 351.90, 347.01, 342.11, 337.22, 333.96) are evenly spaced about 5.6 K apart and 4.9 K apart. They are autoscaled colorbar ticks, not per-block temperatures or a verified hottest-block reading. The extraction's claim that per-block values such as 373.83 K are legible is unsupported. Treating the top tick difference (7.24) as the peak reduction is an inference without visual verification, and the units are not printed.

The Fig. 20 caption says 'for Black', but the text says 'Figure 20 shows spatial thermal variation for Body'. The workload and time-stamp behind the '7 C' statement are ambiguous. The extraction flags this but still pairs the labels with a 7 C reduction.

findings.locator: PDF p.13 (Fig. 15 paragraph), p.14 (RoI sentence), p.9 Sec. 3.2.2, p.5 Sec. 3.1.2

findings.reason: The 20 mV/ns value is supported, but the paper's derived t_vr is about 13 ns for 1.12 V to 0.76 V. At 20 mV/ns, 0.36 V takes 18 ns. The 42-44 ns low-V/F dwell plus 2 x t_vr within the 70 ns stall does not reconcile either. The paper's own timing and energy claims (86-94 nJ, 44 nJ switching) are internally inconsistent and cannot be taken as verified.

A 2M-cycle way-shutdown interval at 3 GHz is about 0.67 ms, but Fig. 19 shows only 500 stamps x 0.33 us, about 165 us, so a way-gating decision and its thermal effect cannot be seen in that window. The paper's transient claims depend on its unpublished gem5/McPAT/HotSpot traces. Any 2D steady reproduction would not reproduce them.
findings.locator: PDF p.13 Sec. 4; p.15 Fig. 19 paragraph

findings.reason: The experiment is declared custom_2d_steady with an empty floorplan and empty power_w while steady_2d_relevant is false and the mismatches are essential (transient, DVFS/way-gating dynamics, no block geometry or power, unpublished package). It must not be treated as a 2D reproduction. Any generated 2D placement or constant power row would be an illustrative assumption, not published data.

337 nJ per 70 ns stall and 0.106/0.168 W regulator overheads are correctly not used as block power rows. They are supported (pp.10, 14), but no same-scenario power exists for any floorplan block (cores, L1, L2 banks, routers), so power coverage of every block cannot be verified.
findings.locator: PDF p.10 Sec. 3.2.2; p.14 Sec. 4; p.13 Sec. 4

assessment.summary: The 2D screening label is not_2d_applicable, and Studio did not run (simulation status: skipped). The gate failed on Studio input validity: the custom_2d_steady experiment has an empty floorplan and no power_w, while the schema requires 1-128 blocks plus a power object. input_gate_pass and scientific_gate_pass are false, simulation_allowed is false, comparison_valid is false, and the result is not independently verified. Because of the gate, the final verdict is no simulation and no numerical comparison. No exact replication is claimed. The paper scenario is WaFFLe on a 16-tile, 32nm 2D CMP using gem5, McPAT and HotSpot 6.0, with LLC way-gating plus per-core fine-grained DVFS. The headline observable is an 8.4 C maximum reduction in peak temperature versus the paper's own baseline (6.2 C for average temperature) on the 8MB LLC. This is a relative reduction from a transient, policy-driven workload. The paper's temperatures were sampled at 0.33 us with way-shutdown at 2M-cycle intervals. A custom 2D steady run would have no transient trace and cannot reproduce this dynamic behavior. No pinned Ascend910 or ATPlace commit, bundled EV6/GCC adaptation, or generated placement was used, so there is no illustrative input.flp or one-row input.ptrace and no source commit to report. The artifact search found no linked code, configs or floorplans. The paper gives no block geometry or per-block watts, and the only stated boundary condition is a 47 C ambient. Studio's package and cooling defaults would differ from the unpublished HotSpot configuration. Any such run would be illustrative only. Numerical comparison would require matching location (hottest on-chip point), aggregation (maximum across nine apps), regime (transient with leakage feedback) and boundary assumptions, and none of these can be matched. At most, a qualitative statement is possible: lowering power during memory stalls and gating cache ways plausibly reduces temperature and leakage. This is not verified here.

No complete experiment is extractable, so the floorplan is empty. If an illustrative run were made, any generated 2D placement and one-row power trace would be separate from paper facts, and its temperatures would not be compared numerically to the paper.
Studio package and material properties (die, TIM, heat spreader, heat sink, convection) are bundled defaults and not the paper's HotSpot 6.0 configuration, which is not published.
Ambient is the only paper-stated thermal boundary condition (47 C, Table 1, PDF p.13). Other boundary conditions would be Studio defaults.
